issues.legal_issue: False records, non-performance of entrusted work, and non-payment of entrusted funds supported convictions for falsifying records, criminal breach of trust, and criminal misconduct.
material_facts: The accused were public employees responsible for work under an improvement scheme and had received funds for that work.
They recorded that rectification work had been done and payments made, although the work had not been done and the funds had not been paid to the labourers.
Site inspections and the accused’s own admissions supported the finding that the records were false and the funds had not been disbursed.
issues.conclusion: The Court found no cogent ground to disturb the findings of guilt or the convictions.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied sections 218, 477A and 409 read with section 34 of the Indian Penal Code, and sections 5(2) and 5(1)(d) of the Prevention of Corruption Act. It upheld the findings that the accused prepared false documents, committed criminal breach of trust, and engaged in criminal misconduct in the discharge of their duties.

rule.if: appeal_against_conviction and entrusted_public_funds and records_claimed_work_or_payment and work_or_payment_not_done

predicates.appeal_against_conviction: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a criminal conviction.
predicates.entrusted_public_funds: Public employees were entrusted with funds to carry out specified public work.
predicates.records_claimed_work_or_payment: The employees made records stating that the specified work had been done or funds had been paid.
predicates.work_or_payment_not_done: The specified work had not been done or the recorded payments had not been made.

issues.definition: When a criminal conviction is appealed and public employees entrusted with funds recorded work or payments that had not occurred, the conviction is upheld.

issues.legal_issue: Later completion of work or disbursement of money does not undo an earlier dishonest misappropriation, even when the misappropriation lasted only temporarily.
material_facts: The accused recorded work as completed and funds as paid when neither had occurred.
After the matter was reported to higher authorities, the accused allegedly completed the work and disbursed the funds for their intended purpose.
issues.conclusion: Subsequent completion of the work or disbursement of the funds did not absolve the accused of criminal liability for the earlier misappropriation.
issues.legal_principle: Explanation 1 to section 403 of the Indian Penal Code provides that dishonest misappropriation for a time only is misappropriation within that section. Later restitution or remedial action does not efface an offence already committed.

predicates.appeal_against_misappropriation_convicti: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a conviction for criminal misappropriation.
predicates.dishonest_misappropriation_occurred: The accused dishonestly appropriated entrusted property, even if only for a limited time.
predicates.later_restoration_after_discovery: The accused restored the property or completed the intended work only after the misconduct came to the attention of others.

issues.definition: If an appeal concerns a dishonest misappropriation and restoration occurs only after discovery, the later restoration does not exonerate the accused.

issues.legal_issue: A completed trial is not invalidated by an unlawful investigation unless the illegality caused prejudice or a miscarriage of justice.
material_facts: The appellants alleged that the investigation had been conducted in breach of the statutory requirements for investigating corruption offences.
The trial had proceeded to completion, and the record did not show that the alleged investigative breach prejudiced the appellants or caused a miscarriage of justice.
issues.conclusion: The alleged breach of the investigation requirements did not justify setting aside the convictions.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 5A of the Prevention of Corruption Act, an investigative illegality does not affect the trial court’s competence or jurisdiction and does not by itself invalidate a completed trial. The conviction may be set aside only if the illegality caused prejudice or a miscarriage of justice. The Court relied on H. N. Rishbud and Inder Singh v. The State of Delhi, [1955] 1 S.C.R. 1150.

predicates.appeal_after_completed_trial: The proceeding is an appeal following a trial that has reached completion.
predicates.investigation_illegality: The investigation was conducted contrary to a legal requirement governing the investigation.
predicates.no_prejudice_or_miscarriage: The investigative illegality did not prejudice the accused or cause a miscarriage of justice.

issues.definition: After a completed trial, an investigative illegality without prejudice or a miscarriage of justice does not result in the conviction being set aside.

issues.legal_issue: A statutory protection and time limit for acts done under an enabling law do not bar prosecution for dishonest acts that were neither done in good faith nor done under that law.
material_facts: The prosecution was instituted more than six months after the acts complained of.
The accused had prepared false records and misappropriated funds entrusted for public work.
The acts were committed in breach of the accused’s duties rather than in the discharge of duties under the improvement-scheme law.
issues.conclusion: The statutory protection and six-month time limit did not bar the prosecution.
issues.legal_principle: Section 23(1) of the Bombay Land Improvement Schemes Act, 1942 protects only things done or intended to be done in good faith under the Act. Section 23(2) applies to things done or intended to be done under the Act; it does not cover conduct that is outside, or in flagrant breach of, the duties imposed by the Act. The Court also referred to the meaning of good faith under the Bombay General Clauses Act.

rule.if: public_servant_prosecution and prosecution_after_limitation_period and not_good_faith and acts_not_under_enabling_law

predicates.public_servant_prosecution: The prosecution is against a public servant for conduct connected with duties assigned under an enabling law.
predicates.prosecution_after_limitation_period: The prosecution was instituted after the period specified by the asserted statutory time limit.
predicates.not_good_faith: The public servant acted dishonestly rather than honestly.
predicates.acts_not_under_enabling_law: The acts were not done in discharging duties under the enabling law but instead breached or disregarded those duties.

issues.definition: When a public servant is prosecuted after the specified period for dishonest acts outside the duties imposed by the enabling law, the statutory time bar does not apply.
